expectations.text: Uses Input for name fields, Textarea for bio, Switch for toggles, Select+Option for frequency
expectations.evidence: Input used for 'First name' and 'Last name' (lines 26-37), Textarea for 'Bio' (lines 40-46), Switch for 'Email notifications' and 'SMS notifications' (lines 56-63), Select+Option for 'Notification frequency' with Daily/Weekly/Monthly options (lines 65-73).

expectations.text: Groups fields into visual sections (headings, Details, or Card sections)
expectations.evidence: Entire form wrapped in <Card> (line 18). Two <section> elements with <h2> headings: 'Profile' (line 23) and 'Notifications' (line 53). Sections separated by <Divider /> components (line 49).

expectations.text: Uses wa-stack for vertical field flow
expectations.evidence: Multiple wa-stack utility classes used: className="wa-stack wa-gap-l" on main wrapper (line 19), className="wa-stack wa-gap-m" on Profile section (line 22) and Notifications section (line 52), className="wa-stack wa-gap-s" on switches container (line 55). These achieve vertical stacking layout.

expectations.text: Select has Option children with value props (Daily, Weekly, Monthly)
expectations.evidence: Lines 65-73 show <Select label="Notification frequency"> with three <Option> children: <Option value="daily">Daily</Option>, <Option value="weekly">Weekly</Option>, <Option value="monthly">Monthly</Option>.

expectations.text: Installs all needed components via npx kigumi add
expectations.evidence: Line 7: 'npx kigumi add Input Textarea Button Select Option Switch Divider Card' covers every component used in the code.

expectations.text: Every form control has a label prop
expectations.evidence: Input has label="First name" and label="Last name". Textarea has label="Bio". Select has label="Notification frequency". However, Switch components (lines 56-62) use children text ('Email notifications', 'SMS notifications') instead of a label prop. Strictly, they lack a label prop.

claims.claim: No custom CSS needed -- layout handled by WA utility classes
claims.evidence: SettingsForm.css is empty (just a comment). All layout uses wa-stack, wa-cluster, wa-gap-*, wa-heading-s, and wa-justify-content-end utility classes. Only inline styles are for Card width (560px) and margin.

claims.claim: First name / Last name sit side-by-side using wa-cluster
claims.evidence: Line 25: <div className="wa-cluster wa-gap-m"> wraps both Input components, each with style={{ flex: 1 }}.
Lines 12-13 show imports from '@/components/ui' and '@/components/ui/Option/Option'. Note the inconsistent import path for Option (direct file import vs barrel export).

suggestions.assertion: Every form control has a label prop
suggestions.reason: This assertion is ambiguous for Switch, which in Web Awesome uses children as its label (not a label prop). The eval should clarify whether children-based labeling counts, or explicitly state 'label prop or visible label text' to avoid false failures for correct patterns.

No assertion checks whether the output avoids className on wa-* elements (a critical Kigumi rule: use class, not className on web components). This output uses className on plain HTML divs and sections, which is fine, but the distinction is not tested.

No assertion verifies the import paths are correct. The output imports Option from '@/components/ui/Option/Option' separately from other components, which may indicate the barrel export was missed or the agent was unsure. This kind of structural issue goes unchecked.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover component selection and layout patterns well. The label-prop assertion could be more precise about Switch's labeling pattern. Consider adding an assertion for import correctness since that is a common failure mode.
